title: Research, statistics & ethics
objectives: Rank study designs by evidence level and name each design's signature bias.
Interpret p-values, confidence intervals, sensitivity/specificity and ROC thinking.
State consent, assent and ethics-committee requirements for paediatric research.
body_md:
### Why this area matters

One predictable question per exam cycle, and the easiest distinction-level marks available: designs, biases, basic stats, ethics. Clinicians underprepare it; you will not.

### Designs and biases

Case report < case series < case-control (recall bias, odds ratio) < cohort (loss to follow-up, relative risk) < RCT (allocation concealment, intention-to-treat) < systematic review/meta-analysis. Diagnostic-accuracy studies need STARD-style thinking: blinding, consecutive spectrum, reference standard. Bias word-bank: selection, recall, lead-time and length-time (screening), publication, confounding — define each with its fix (randomisation, blinding, stratification, matching).

### Statistics that actually get asked

P-value as incompatibility with the null, not truth probability; confidence intervals as precision; power and sample-size drivers (effect size, variance, alpha, power); sensitivity/specificity versus predictive values (prevalence-dependent); ROC curves trading sensitivity against specificity. Read a 2×2 table fluently and the question answers itself.

### Ethics and medico-legal

Paediatric research needs ethics-committee approval, parental consent plus child assent by age and maturity, minimal-risk justification, and data confidentiality. Clinical ethics Army: best interests, Gillick-type competence for adolescents, second opinions in DSD and oncology, honest counselling with documentation. Medico-legal answers cover consent validity, negligence (duty, breach, causation, damage), record-keeping and MLC documentation in trauma.

### How it is asked

Define → rank → apply to a vignette → state the ethical call. Short structured answers outscore long ones here; use the word-bank deliberately.
